findings.text: The mid-ingest protection the plan relies on is enforced at planning time, not at deletion time. PLAN_INCLUDED excludes a file whose n.claimed_at is within DEFAULT_CLAIM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s) and freezes the surviving ids into to_delete.json; cmd_delete then deletes exactly that frozen list about 2 minutes later without re-evaluating the claim predicate. A CodeFile that acquires a live ingest claim between plan and delete would still have its freshly written CodeExample/CodeChunk deleted, the outcome the plan's 'excludes any file holding a live claim, so a file mid-ingest keeps its new chunks' intends to prevent. No file was excluded at run time (to_delete.json exclusions == {}, plan 09:26 vs delete 09:28), so no harm occurred here; a re-run of cmd_delete from a stale to_delete.json inherits the same gap. One-line fix: re-apply the PLAN_INCLUDED claim predicate inside DELETE_CYPHER.

The implemented node set is 'CodeFile whose status <> ingested AND carries a chunk' (CARRIES EXISTS), but plan section 27 reads 'deletes the CodeExample and CodeChunk nodes of every CodeFile whose status is not ingested'. A file below ingested whose CodeFile <-FROM_FILE CodeExample carries no CodeChunk is outside the node set, and the cascade itself only reaches examples through HAS_CHUNK, so such a chunk-less stale CodeExample survives. I measured exactly one: jet CodeFile jet:/home/dvanees/Local_BIS_n_Exp_BIS_MATLAB/Local_BIS_n_exp_BIS_July2013ManyCasesVersion.m (status failed) retains CodeExample jet:Local_BIS_n_exp_BIS_July2013ManyCasesVersion:9583765e with zero chunks (probe ORPHAN_EXAMPLES = 1 file / 1 example, ATTACHED shows 0 chunks). The plan's stated done-when is chunk-focused ('no file below ingested carries a chunk') and is met, so this is a residual of the prose scope, not a done-when failure.

The fragment's 'CodeExamples deleted' column (826/373/53) reproduces the planned code_example_ids lengths from to_delete.json, and the delete log's files=N is count(n) of matched CodeFiles (DELETE_CYPHER returns count(n), and the cascade is a FOREACH DETACH DELETE that returns no per-node count), so neither is a measured count of deleted CodeExample nodes. The chunk removal is independently confirmed by the residual verify (my re-run: RESIDUAL [] with the CONTROL arm reading 68587 files / 266231 chunks, so the instrument sees the graph), but the example-deleted count is inferred from the plan, not observed. The file also has no trailing newline.
